'''Karen Dee Ann Shuman Michalowicz''' (died 2006) was an American [[middle school]] mathematics teacher.{{r|wapo}} She was known for her advocacy of incorporating the [[history of mathematics]], [[women in mathematics]], and [[ethnomathematics]] into [[mathematics education]] as a way to encourage greater diversity and inclusion in mathematics,{{r|conv}} and for her collection of old textbooks, including works by [[Nicolo Tartaglia]], [[Georg Sabinus]], and [[Christopher Clavius]] published in the 16th century.{{r|wapo|amu}}

==Education and career==
Karen Shuman was born in [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]], the daughter of a [[United States Marine Corps]] serviceman. She was educated in [[Falls Church, Virginia]], [[Jakarta]], Indonesia, and a Catholic high school in [[Alexandria, Virginia]]. She received her bachelor's degree from the [[Catholic University of America]], and a master's degree from the [[University of Virginia]].{{r|wapo}}

She worked as a middle school mathematics teacher in [[McLean, Virginia]] "for nearly 40 years",{{r|wapo}} known as "Ms. Mikey" to her students.{{r|wapo|imo}} She chaired the upper school mathematics department at The Langley School, a private school in McLean.{{r|wapo|amu}} She also held an adjunct professorship at [[George Mason University]], served on the board of [[Mathcounts]], was a member of the National Commission on Mathematics Instruction of the [[National Research Council (United States)|National Research Council]],{{r|wapo}} served as an editor for the [[Mathematical Association of America]] journal ''Convergence'', and co-directed a [[National Science Foundation]] project, "Historical Modules for the Teaching and Learning of Mathematics".{{r|conv}}

Her students at The Langley School included Nathan Curtis,{{r|wapo|imo}} who went on to receive silver and gold medals in the 1996 and 1997 [[International Mathematical Olympiad]]{{r|curtis}} and who credited Michalowicz with sparking his interest in mathematics.{{r|wapo|imo}}

==Personal life==
She married Joseph Michalowicz on June 8, 1963;{{r|wed}} they had two children. They divorced but she kept his name. She settled in Falls Church, where she was a parishioner of [[List of churches in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Arlington|Saint Anthony of Padua Falls Church]], a local Catholic church.{{r|wapo}}

She died of [[bone marrow cancer]] on July 17, 2006.{{r|wapo|conv}}

==Recognition and legacy==
Michalowicz was a 1990 recipient of the [[Presidential Award for Excellence in Mathematics and Science Teaching]]. She was also named State Teacher of the Year for Virginia by the [[American Association of University Women]], and teacher of the year by the Virginia Council of Teachers of Mathematics.{{r|wapo}}

Her book collection is held in the library of [[American University]].{{r|amu}} The Virginia Council of Teachers of Mathematics offers a grant named for Michalowicz for travel to conferences of the [[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics]].{{r|grant}}
